take: An AI hardware selloff defined the week, with tech down 8.2% and the Nasdaq down 3.4%, while energy fell 12.0% as WTI crude dropped 12.8%. Democrats winning Congress sparked a broad Wednesday rally, but Thursday's de-risking pushed the VIX up 59% in a day and moved the market regime to Stressed. Abroad, Europe was nearly flat as the Stoxx 600 gained 0.2%, while chip-heavy Asian markets were hit hard, with the Kospi down 11.7% and the Nikkei down 9.3%, even as the Hang Seng rose 5.1%. Your portfolio fell 0.98%, beating the S&P 500's 2.68% drop by about 1.7 points but trailing the Conservative benchmark's 0.40% decline by about 0.6 points. AMZN (+7.88%) and MCD (+7.13%, after an earnings beat) each added about half a point. SCHG (-0.59 pts) and CRM (-0.42 pts, likely weighed in part by its share offering filing) took back most of those gains, a sign that the portfolio's growth tilt likely explains the gap to the Conservative benchmark.
lesson_title: What a jumping VIX tells you
lesson: The VIX measures how much movement investors expect in the S&P 500 over the next month, based on options prices, so it rises when people pay up for protection. This week it fell to 17.20 after the election rally, then jumped 59% to 26.47 on Thursday as tech sank 7.24%, finishing the week up 32%. At the same time the 10-year yield fell 7 bps and gold rose 4.5%, a typical flight-to-safety pattern where fear lifts the VIX and money moves toward bonds and gold.
